plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a steady ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating in stable assets. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy HOOD at 4% and GOOGL at 4% to add high-scoring, quality tech names.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month growth by blending broad index, quality tech, and limited leverage. It aims for a risk-first approach, reducing concentration while still seeking growth opportunities. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Add to SOXL, bringing it to 10%, and SPAL to 5%, increasing leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to CRWD, bringing it to 15%, to press a high-performing asset.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by leveraging high-scoring setups and increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware of daily decay/rebalancing in leveraged ETFs and the potential for rapid, substantial losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions from income/covered-call ETFs. It aims for low drawdown and reliable income, but distributions are variable and NAV can still fall. This is for cash-like income, not a savings account.
